question.problem:
The joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ for the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given in the table below. Find $\text{E}[\operatorname{cos}⁡(X+Y)].$

| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=\frac{\pi }{2}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.5$ | $0.25$ |
| $X=\frac{\pi }{2}$ | $0.05$ | $0.2$ |
question.worked_solution:
Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are discrete random variables with supports ${S}_{X}$ and ${S}_{Y},$ respectively, and $f(x,y)$ is their joint probability mass function with support $S={S}_{X}\times {S}_{Y}.$ If $r:{R}^{2}\to R$ is a function of two variables, then the rule of the lazy statistician states that

$$
\text{E}[r(X,Y)]={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}r(x,y)\,f(x,y).
$$

In our case, we have

$$
r(x,y)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y).
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[\operatorname{cos}⁡(X+Y)] & ={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}r(x,y)\,f(x,y) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(0+0)\cdot f(0,0)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(0+\frac{\pi }{2})\cdot f(0,\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & \,+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}+0)\cdot f(\frac{\pi }{2},0)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}+\frac{\pi }{2})\cdot f(\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)\cdot f(0,0)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})\cdot f(0,\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & \,+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})\cdot f(\frac{\pi }{2},0)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )\cdot f(\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =1\cdot 0.5+0\cdot 0.25+0\cdot 0.05+(-1)\cdot 0.2 \\  & =0.5+0+0-0.2 \\  & =0.3.\end{aligned}
$$
